---
title: End a turn with a host notice
description: Deliver a host decision through the output policy and find its author in the saved conversation.
---

When your application reaches a request cap, it can supply the reply itself. Enable
`hostEndedTurns` when constructing the agent, then call `endTurn` when the host makes
its decision. The host can send a notice without inventing a user message.

<CodeFile path="examples/deploy/host-ended-turn.ts" region="host-ended-turn" title="Deliver a host notice" />

Run the example locally with `npm run example examples/deploy/host-ended-turn.ts`.
The result shows the delivered text, the author `host` and the run ID saved with that
assistant entry. The mock provider throws if called, so a successful run also checks
that the notice used no model call.

Use the string returned by `endTurn` for display. Output middleware can rewrite the
candidate or refuse it. If the turn needs a model judge, use an ordinary model turn.
To preserve real inbound text, pass `{ message }` as the second argument. A host with
an `aroundTurn` wrapper requires that input. To continue a saved conversation, pass
`{ continueFrom: checkpoint }` there as well. See [Conversations](./conversations).

Cancellation before delivery leaves the notice out of the stream, checkpoint and
episodic stores. Once the terminal checks pass, the stream and checkpoint receive
the admitted wording. The saved `agent.turn_end` event identifies the host as
`replyAuthor` and carries the run ID. The configured episodic window writers then
run in order, while this turn still owns the agent.

Each writer reports `agentfootprint.memory.write_outcome` with its memory ID.
`acknowledged` means the writer completed. `unknown` means it could have stored
some, all or none of the messages. A later cancellation or lost acknowledgment
leaves the delivered reply intact. Read the outcome for each store before retrying a write.
